entities.summary: Ghiyāth al-Dīn Jamshīd Masʿūd al-Kāshī was a Persian astronomer and mathematician during the reign of Tamerlane. Born in the late 14th century, al-Kāshī was a prominent scholar of the time, known for his expertise in astronomy, mathematics, and Islamic theology. He was appointed as the chief astronomer of Samarkand in 1404, a position he held until his death in 1429. Al-Kāshī made significant contributions to the field of astronomy, including the calculation of the sine of the angle between the equator and the celestial equator. His work built upon the discoveries of earlier scholars, such as Ulugh Beg, and laid the foundation for future astronomical discoveries. Al-Kāshī's legacy extends beyond his scientific contributions, as he was also a prominent figure in the cultural and intellectual life of the Timurid Empire. His writings and teachings had a profound impact on the development of Islamic thought and learning. Al-Kāshī's life and work serve as a testament to the enduring power of human curiosity and the importance of preserving knowledge for future generations. The precise calculations he made allowed for more accurate astronomical observations and had a profound impact on the development of the field. Al-Kāshī's contributions to the field of astronomy paved the way for future breakthroughs and discoveries. His legacy continues to inspire astronomers and scholars to this day.

entities.summary: Ghiyāth al-Dīn Jamshīd Masʿūd al-Kāshī was a Persian astronomer and mathematician who played a crucial role in the development of Islamic astronomy during the reign of Tamerlane. Born in 1380 in Kashan, Persia (modern-day Iran), al-Kāshī was a polymath who made significant contributions to the fields of trigonometry, algebra, and astronomy. His most notable work, the Zij al-Soltanī, a comprehensive astronomical table, was completed in 1429 and remains an important reference for Islamic astronomers to this day. Al-Kāshī's legacy extends beyond his mathematical and astronomical achievements, as he helped to bridge the cultural and scientific divide between the Islamic world and Europe. His works influenced European scholars, including Regiomontanus, and paved the way for the transmission of Arabic scientific knowledge to the West. Al-Kāshī's significance lies in his role as a bridge between East and West, demonstrating the importance of cultural exchange and the transmission of knowledge across borders. Through his works, al-Kāshī left a lasting impact on the development of astronomy and mathematics, and his legacy continues to inspire scholars and scientists today.
